question: After matching plant family and native range, does any butterfly-specific host-identity expansion excess remain when null host prominence is calibrated to reproduce the observed mean number of other Lepidoptera consumers per host?
focal_panel: Same 207-species strict host-bias panel with adequate host taxonomy and sufficient alternative same-family HOSTS-WCVP candidate hosts.
exact_constraints: number of hosts in each WCVP plant family
observed focal hosts excluded from alternatives
sampling without replacement within each focal portfolio
prominence_target: Mean number of other Lepidoptera species recorded using observed hosts in the strict-null focal panel.
calibration: For each native-range bandwidth, choose the degree-weight exponent by deterministic bisection so the median null mean other-Lepidoptera degree matches the observed target. Calibration uses only host-network degree, not plant expansion outcomes.
primary_endpoints: total introduced-added species x WGSRPD3 units
secondary_endpoint: Spearman host-family breadth vs log resource expansion
interpretation_rule: If observed expansion is not above the prominence-calibrated null across all three native-range bandwidths, the simple same-family host-identity excess is not identifiable beyond starting geography and network prominence.
claim_boundary: This is post-hoc and calibrates to HOSTS consumer degree, which remains a joint proxy for ecological host prominence/commonness and study/recording intensity. It cannot partition those components or establish a causal role of prominence in plant introduction.
